hero.filename: OFFICE OF THE HELEN MOUNTAIN EAGLE, A MONTHLY NEWSPAPER PUBLISHED IN HELEN, GEORGIA, NEAR ROBERTSTOWN - NARA - 557682.jpg
hero.caption: Scope and content:  OFFICE OF THE HELEN MOUNTAIN EAGLE, A MONTHLY NEWSPAPER PUBLISHED IN HELEN, GEORGIA, NEAR ROBERTSTOWN. IT IS EDITED AND PUBLISHED BY PHIL GARNER (STANDING), A WRITER FOR THE ATLANTA JOURNAL AND CONSTITUTION WITH THE HELP OF HIS WIFE, RIGHT, AND ONE ASSISTANT, LEFT. THE FIRST EDITION OF THE NEWSPAPER/MAGAZINE WAS PUBLISHED IN JUNE, 1975, THE FIRST PERIODICAL FOR HELEN IN MORE THAN 30 YEARS. THE GARNERS AND THEIR TWO CHILDREN ARRIVE IN HELEN EVERY WEEKEND AND HOPE TO BECOME PERMANENT RESIDENTS SOON

images.filename: AERIAL VIEW OF HELEN, GEORGIA, NEAR ROBERTSTOWN, SHOWING GEORGIA HIGHWAY 17-75 LEADING INTO TOWN FROM THE SOUTH - NARA - 557651.jpg
images.caption: Scope and content:  AERIAL VIEW OF HELEN, GEORGIA, NEAR ROBERTSTOWN, SHOWING GEORGIA HIGHWAY 17/75 LEADING INTO TOWN FROM THE SOUTH. HELEN WAS A TYPICAL GEORGIA MOUNTAIN VILLAGE UNTIL EARLY 1969 WHEN LOCAL OFFICIALS, BUSINESSMEN AND RESIDENTS APPROVED THE IDEA OF A BAVARIAN ALPINE VILLAGE MOTIF THAT COULD BE APPLIED TO EXTERIORS OF EXISTING BUILDINGS. TOURISM HAS ENABLED THE TOWN OF SOME 270 PEOPLE TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL SUPPORT SERVICES. A DEVELOPMENT PLAN CAUTIONS ABOUT THE NEED FOR BALANCE BETWEEN COMMERCIALISM AND PUBLIC INTEREST

images.filename: FRITZ BACHMAN, A GLASSBLOWER, WHO LIVES IN HELEN, GEORGIA NEAR ROBERTSTOWN - NARA - 557678.jpg
images.caption: Scope and content:  FRITZ BACHMAN, A GLASSBLOWER, WHO LIVES IN HELEN, GEORGIA NEAR ROBERTSTOWN. HE MOVED TO THE VILLAGE OF 270 INHABITANTS WITH HIS TWO CHILDREN UN 1973. BACHMAN WAS ATTRACTED TO HELEN AFTER THE TOWN's SMALL BUSINESS DISTRICT WAS RENOVATED WITH A BAVARIAN ALPINE THEME. HE HAS A SHOP IN THE HELEN THEATER BUILDING ON MAIN STREET THE RENOVATION HAS INCREASED COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT AND BROUGHT TOURISM TO WHAT WAS A TYPICAL SMALL MOUNTAIN COMMUNITY PRIOR TO 1969. BACHMAN IS A NATIVE OF THURINGEN, GERMANY
